provenance.instrument: Code of the Township of Tredyffrin, Chapter 208 Zoning, as published on eCode360, with 208 Attachment 1 (R-4 area and bulk table)
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 (code TR1485): includes legislation through 09-21-2026. New Laws: a charter amendment (2026-05-20) and a vehicles and traffic amendment (2026-10-19), neither in Chapter 208. Recent Chapter 208 amendments (Ord. HR-474 2023, HR-490 and HR-491 2025) touch the historic overlay demolition rules, office conversions and site development, not the residence district uses. Read in the eCode360 print views in a browser on 2026-11-12.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: Includes legislation through 09-21-2026. New Laws: none for Chapter 208.
checks: No general accessory dwelling unit rule. RC, R-1/2, R-1, R-2, R-3 and R-4 allow the listed uses 'and no other' and one single-family detached dwelling (208-12, 208-17, 208-21, 208-25, 208-29, 208-33)

On a property with a historic resource on the Historic Resources Map, an 'accessory apartment' is allowed by conditional use (Board of Supervisors) after a Historical Commission recommendation. It may be in an accessory structure only if that structure is a contributing resource. It is the only other dwelling unit. 2 off-street spaces (208-122.6B(1)(d))

As an accessory use in every residence district, an 'accessory apartment for a watchman, caretaker or the staff or employees of a permitted use' is allowed, subject to the RC area and height rules of 208-13 (208-12G(2)). It is not a general rental unit

A house that existed when the chapter took effect may be converted to two-family or multifamily use (four units at most) by special exception. The lot needs the district minimum times the number of families (208-106)
A building with more than one set of cooking facilities counts as more than one dwelling unit (208-6 'Dwelling unit')
One rental room for up to two boarders, without housekeeping privileges, is a permitted accessory use (208-12G(3))
Accessory buildings over 144 sq ft or 10 ft high meet the district yards and height. None between the house and the street (208-112A(1))
R-4 allows a two-family detached dwelling (duplex) by special exception after Planning Commission review, 6,000 sq ft per unit (208-33E(2), 208 Attachment 1)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Tredyffrin Township Zoning Officer, Zoning Hearing Board, Board of Supervisors (conditional uses), Historical Commission. Census GEOID from towns_index.json. Searched the full Chapter 208 print view for: accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, in-law, granny, ECHO, elder cottage, carriage house, guest house, caretaker, servant, second dwelling, secondary dwelling, accessory unit, family member, short-term, conversion, similar, not listed. No section sends unlisted uses to a hearing. Short-term rentals in a historic structure are a special exception in R-1/2 (208-17E(7)).

term.note: 208-6 'APARTMENT, ACCESSORY': 'One dwelling unit which is incidental and subordinate to the principal use of a building on a lot which may be either a separate living unit for a member of the family or other relatives, servants or caretakers in a residence' or a unit with a nonresidential use. The definition reaches family, but the only general listing is the Historic Resource Overlay (conditional use). Elsewhere the use is listed only for a watchman, caretaker or staff (208-12G(2)), so a family accessory apartment is defined but not listed.

status.note: No general ADU rule. The residence districts allow the listed uses 'and no other'. Only a property with a historic resource has an accessory apartment path (conditional use, 208-122.6B(1)(d)).

path.note: 'Land and buildings may be used and occupied for any one of the following purposes and no other'. A second unit on a house lot that is not a conversion or a historic accessory apartment needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

fallback_path.note: A lot that fails a district rule also needs a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

historic_path.note: On a property with a historic resource that has street access: 'Accessory apartment' after a Historical Commission recommendation and conditional use approval from the Board of Supervisors. No family or owner rule. Conditions in gates.

value.conditions: Only a house that existed when the chapter took effect. At most four units. Parking per 208-103. The Board sets the number of families.

value.name: Accessory apartment for a watchman, caretaker or staff of a permitted use
value.conditions: Only for a watchman, caretaker or the staff or employees of a permitted use. A live-in paid caregiver may fit 'staff or employees'. Subject to the RC area and height rules of 208-13 (5 acres, 300 ft wide, 35 ft high), as the text reads.
value.note: Employee housing, not a general ADU. Whether household staff of a house count, and whether the 5 acre RC lot applies in other districts, is a reading. Ask the zoning officer.

alternatives.note: Not ADUs. 208-106: 'a single-family detached dwelling, existing at the effective date of this chapter, may be converted into and used as a two-family or a multifamily dwelling for no more than four dwelling units when authorized as a special exception'.

zoning_districts.note: No district lists a general ADU. The historic accessory apartment follows the Historic Resources Map, not a district.

historic_bypass.note: The Historic Resource Overlay adds an accessory apartment for properties with a historic resource. Confirm the property is on the Historic Resources Map.

value.condition: The property has a historic resource on the Historic Resources Map and access from a street. It may be used for 'any one of' the listed uses (bed-and-breakfast, cultural studio, gallery or museum, accessory apartment), so only one of them. Historical Commission recommendation and Board of Supervisors conditional use approval.
The apartment may be in a structure accessory to the house only if the Board finds that structure a contributing resource shown on the Historic Resource Map.
'The accessory apartment can be the only other single-family dwelling unit on the property.'

In a residence district: new parking seen from neighbors screened to 4 ft, no display or sign beyond 2 sq ft, no noise at the property line, shielded lighting. Floor area added to the historic resource after January 1, 2011 does not count.

On a historic resource the district building area, impervious and yard rules may be modified by up to 15% by conditional use after a Historical Commission recommendation, more where essential to preserve the resource. Added building area may not exceed 50% of the resource's building area.
Accessory buildings over 144 sq ft or 10 ft high meet the district yards and height, and stand behind the house (not between the house and the street).

gates.note: Historic Resource Overlay conditions apply only on the historic path.

types_allowed.note: Historic path only. The apartment is in the house or 'in a structure accessory to the principal dwelling' that is a contributing resource. New buildings and additions are not addressed. No form is allowed off the historic path.

max_height_ft.note: An accessory building over 144 sq ft or 10 ft must meet the district height (35 ft).

accessory_height_applies.note: The 10 ft rule is only for buildings up to 144 sq ft. A building large enough for a unit takes the district height.

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'Any building exceeding 144 square feet or 10 feet in height must meet the yard and height regulations of the zoning district in which it is located.'

setback_side_ft.note: 6 ft only for buildings up to 144 sq ft and 10 ft. Larger ones take the district side yard.

setback_rear_ft.note: 6 ft only for buildings up to 144 sq ft and 10 ft. Larger ones take the district rear yard.

setback_front_ft.note: Accessory buildings are not allowed between the house and any street line.

separation_ft.note: No distance between buildings set for accessory buildings.

owner_occupancy.note: No owner rule for the historic accessory apartment.

family_only.note: No family rule for the historic accessory apartment. A family allows up to three unrelated persons.

short_term_rental_banned.note: Short-term rentals in a historic structure are a special exception in R-1/2 (208-17E(7)) and R-1 (208-21D(7)). Other rules not read.

max_adus.note: Historic path: the apartment 'can be the only other single-family dwelling unit on the property.' Off that path no ADU is allowed.

spaces_required.note: Historic Resource Overlay accessory apartment only: 'Two off-street parking spaces shall be required for the accessory apartment.' The house needs 2 more (208-103C(1)).

total_on_site.note: Historic path: 2 for the house and 2 for the apartment.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached: 10,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, 60 ft wide (208 Attachment 1). Impervious 30%.
